# Pkl 0.32.0 IntSeq Java authority

This fixture records independent calls to the pinned Pkl 0.32.0 Java public API. The canonical `cases.json` and `queries.tsv` contain **237 string calls**, all evaluated in order in each of two fresh JVM sessions with module URI `file:///stage61/intseq-values.pkl`. The observed vector is 198 successes and 39 ordinary Pkl errors. The three typed export calls are a **separate producer-only supplement** in `export-cases.json` and `export-queries.tsv`; all three produce ordinary Pkl export rejection errors in each of two other fresh JVM sessions. A string candidate must compare all 237 canonical rows; export rows are not string comparison passes.

The archive stores complete process protocols, row status, UTF-8 and UTF-16 code unit channels, Java exception and cause metadata, the exact Java helper and runner, authored inputs, pinned upstream source closure, JAR and JDK identities, requested environment and JVM flags, before/after hashes, and both raw repetitions. `tools/int_seq_values_fixtures.py` checks the complete archive offline. `archive-identity.json` and `manifest.json` seal archive membership and fixture files.

The matrix covers constructor and step behavior, properties, equality/hash, representation, iteration, conversion, fold/map callbacks, generators and spread, Bytes bridges, Any and diagnostics, including bounded 64-bit extreme cases. Upstream original IntSeq/Bytes/Any snippets and related source are preserved as source evidence; this authored matrix does not claim those original modules were replayed. Iterator/listing behavior and generator-for behavior can differ at wrapping 64-bit extremes and are recorded as separate calls. The earlier 240-row mixed exploration capture is retained in `target/m2/stage61-intseq-oracle-01` as historical evidence; this fixture uses the subsequently reviewed all-string and all-export captures.

These are Java observations only. Rust native, browser, Node, typed candidate export, full-language compatibility, and performance remain separate checks.
